items.title: Harold Dejan Interview, 1960-10-14
items.q: He and I had a personal friend of mine. We'd come up together, very personal friend of mine.

ctx.x: Another thing you were telling us was that Earl Bostic, you say, got a lot of his stuff from you now.

Well, Earl Bostic was very fast on the saxophone. Very fast. Very good musician and everything. But the style he played on the record, that's the style that Thereto Poino used to play around here. Yeah. That's the style. Every time I heard Earl Bostic's record, I said that. That's right. Have you seen Pernell lately or? I saw him at the banquet we had. Oh, yeah.
Somebody else thought maybe told me that he's recovering a little bit now.

items.title: Theodore Purnell Interview, 1961-02-03
items.q: In the never band, you played baritone.

ctx.x: You know, that's what I said. Well, that's why they hired me at the Japanese T-Guard. Because I was just not clear. I'd hold a note, see, when they finished playing, I'd hold a note. Do it, then it's not the right key, you know. Couldn't make no jazz. I didn't know if I could read that. Yeah. That's right. But I tell you, in them days, it helped so much. Now you take this fella, like Hickman, he could play a little saxophone, but he couldn't read so much, you see. And we was playing next door to one another. And…

Hold that door on the air. Always could read. That's all he could do, read. That fellow, boy, that fellow. Always could read. You buy that piece of music, that was it. That was it. Always could read. In the never band, you played baritone.
Baritone, tenor, alto, tenor. Yeah, yeah. Never band. I didn't buy none of them.
